source_en: Home from my docks office. Logistics.
Back to my estate after a "merger."
Collecting private "medical supplies."
Moving goods somewhere safer.
Testing the loyalty of my "employees."
Moving assets to an underground vault.
Back to my shelter under the grain exchange.
Home to count my remaining holdings.
Collecting what my tenants owe.
Begging my landlord for more time on rent.
Collecting my welfare pension supplement.
Applying as a janitor at the mall.
Queuing for bread. No savings left.
Moving into the evacuee dormitory. Nowhere else.
Reporting my illegal earnings at the tax office.
Handing my deeds to the militia, as ordered.
Dockhand shift. Paid by the crate.
Volunteering at the church soup kitchen, unpaid.
Relax, officer. I'm just a businessman coming home.
Don't smudge the ink. I'm a man who likes things clean.
The world is changing. Men like me always stay on top.
Problem with the date? I'm sure we can reach an… understanding.
When this city is ash, I'll still be holding the shovel.
Stamping that is the smartest thing you'll do today. Don't disappoint me.
Smart move. You might actually survive the week.
I'll remember your face when the new order comes.
You're learning. Too bad there's no time left.
Enjoy this. Nobody puts me in a box twice.
I have friends everywhere. This room will feel crowded by morning.
You have no idea… what you've… just started…
Even death… is just… a transaction…
Where are you coming from?
The docks. Import and logistics, as the permit says. Now stamp it.
One of my warehouses. Moving goods somewhere safer. Six districts to watch.
My shelter under the grain exchange. The count came up short. Careful.
The tram depot. I drive the number four. Honest work, officer.
My brother's in Leningrad. Moved here last week. Nothing here is mine.
My flat. One rented room. Never owned property. I'm a simple man.
Are you experiencing any symptoms?
I don't get sick. Sick men don't last in my line of work.
A cough. Dock air, not whatever you're writing. Choose your next word.
I don't discuss my health with a man holding a stamp. I'm standing.
A weak chest since childhood. The polyclinic sees me weekly.
No cough. I've never set foot on the docks. The air's poison.
Nothing. I'm twenty-five, officer. The body heals itself.
Smart uniform. I hope there's a smart man wearing it.
You have a family, I assume. Hold onto that.
I own three blocks that used to belong to the state. Funny, that.
You're still at your post. Good. That means you're useful.
When the dust settles, I'll still be here. Will you?
I control what's left. That's not a threat. Simply a fact.
